bull.b: Securing 11 MW of contracted power through 2030 strengthens the company’s operating base for mining and future HPC workloads. The zero company share of capital costs and avoided capacity levy improve infrastructure economics while preserving room for longer-term capacity expansion.

Repaying the Bitcoin-backed facility materially improves balance-sheet flexibility by removing substantial secured debt, collateral exposure, and associated interest and collar expenses. This should reduce financing complexity and leave more operational assets available to support future growth initiatives.

Replacing older equipment with more efficient Antminers can increase productive output without proportionate power consumption. The planned hashrate growth and stated incremental revenue capacity support better utilization of existing energized sites and strengthen the mining platform’s operating potential.

bear.b: The recent income statement shows deteriorating unit economics rather than merely slower growth. Falling revenue combined with negative gross profit and exceptionally deep net losses weakens the company’s ability to fund expansion internally and raises uncertainty around the sustainability of its operating model.

Materially negative operating and free cash flow indicate that current activities are consuming cash instead of self-funding operations and investment. Continued burn can constrain deployment of mining and HPC capacity and increase reliance on financing or asset monetization over the coming quarters.

The AI/HPC pivot has strategic appeal but has not yet demonstrated commercial traction. With no Q2 revenue and only immaterial near-term revenue expected, the initiative remains dependent on securing customers, capital, and successful execution before it can materially diversify or improve results.
